title: Big fppf sites contain schemes with bounded open covers
statement: Fix a big fppf site $\mathit{Sch}_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], with its chosen full category of schemes (so all scheme morphisms between its objects are morphisms of this category), and an object $T$ in it; use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme $Z$, put $s(Z)=\max\{\aleph_0,|\mathcal B(Z)|,\sup_{U\in\mathcal B(Z)}|\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Z)|\}$, where $\mathcal B(Z)$ is its set of affine open subschemes and $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Z)$ is the ring of sections of its structure sheaf on $U$. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with an open covering $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$, where $I$ is a set and the $U_i$ have their induced open subscheme structures. If $|I|\leq s(T)^{\aleph_0}$ and $s(U_i)\leq s(T)^{\aleph_0}$ for every $i$, then there exists an object $X_0$ of the chosen category and an isomorphism of schemes $X_0\cong X$. The index set may be empty (then $X$ is the empty scheme).

source.place: Tag 000R, lemma-what-is-in-it, (6); Tag 000J, lemma-construct-category, (2); Tag 000Q, lemma-bound-size. The empty-cover case uses s(empty)=aleph_0 directly. Big-site category specified in topologies.tex, Tag 021R, definition-big-fppf-site.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-scheme-size-open-cover-bound to the given open cover, with no finiteness requirement. It gives $s(X)\leq M$, where $M=\max\{\aleph_0,|I|,\sup_{i\in I}s(U_i)\}$. Its statement includes the empty index set, so this application also covers $X=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 000Q, lemma-bound-size; empty-cover correction as stated in the cited node.

proof.text: Put $\kappa=s(T)$ and $K=\kappa^{\aleph_0}$. By the definition of $s$, $\aleph_0\leq\kappa$, and constant sequences give $\kappa\leq K$. The two hypotheses give $|I|\leq K$ and $\sup_i s(U_i)\leq K$ (also for the empty supremum $0$). Thus $M\leq K$ and step 1 gives $s(X)\leq K\leq\max\{K,\kappa^+\}=B(s(T))$.

source.place: Tag 000R, lemma-what-is-in-it, proof of (6); equation-bound preceding Tag 000J.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-big-site-bounded-size-representative with the fixed big site, its given object $T$, and $Z=X$. The sole size hypothesis was proved in step 2; the cited statement applies to this already chosen category. It supplies an object $X_0$ in that category and an isomorphism $X_0\cong X$, as required.
